sources.entry: magika - Detects file content types with a deep-learning model.

summary.one_liner: Magika is a deep-learning file type detector that identifies the content type of files from their bytes, with a CLI in Rust and Python, JavaScript, and Rust bindings.
summary.what_it_does: Magika uses a small custom neural network (a few MB) to predict the content type of a file, covering 200+ binary and textual types. It reads only a limited subset of each file's content, so inference time stays roughly constant regardless of file size. It can identify files from paths, raw bytes, or streams, and the CLI can scan many files at once or recurse through directories with -r. Output can be a description, MIME type, simple label, score, JSON/JSONL, or a custom format. A per-content-type threshold system falls back to generic labels such as "Generic text document" when the model is not confident, and prediction modes (high-confidence, medium-confidence, best-guess) control how tolerant detection is to errors.
use_cases: identify unknown file types from content rather than extension
route files to security or content scanners
detect file type of uploaded files in a web service
pipe file contents through a command line type check
detect file types inside a Python script
notable: Small model (a few MB) that classifies files in milliseconds on a single CPU
Trained on ~100M samples across 200+ content types, about 99% average precision and recall per the README
Per-content-type thresholds fall back to generic labels when unsure
Used at scale by Google to route Gmail, Drive, and Safe Browsing files, per the README
Web demo runs locally in the browser
caveats: Go bindings are described as work in progress
JavaScript npm package is described as experimental
Not an official Google product and not supported by Google, per the disclaimer
